Adaptive Idle Analyzer v3.3 · Reference behavior

The analyzer is a diagnostic workbench: select evidence → diagnose → propose a next test → compare follow-up logs. It never treats one log as proof of a particular tuning change.

Adaptive modes: Stability, Base Airflow, RPM PID, DC Valve Tracking, DC Bias / Position PID, Ignition, Load Recovery and Compare. Each changes the main plotted signals, summary metrics, hypotheses and next-test guidance.

Timeline: Automatically discovered regions use RPM ≤ threshold plus optional TPS/CLT qualification. Each segment has its own color. Click an interval to focus the chart; drag on unused space to add a manual range. Use Manage regions to enable, exclude, resize, split, merge or remove manual regions.

Analyzing: Only enabled intervals contribute to aggregate results. Changing interval/qualification marks the last analysis stale until Run Analysis is pressed. The highlighted region controls graph focus, not which regions are analyzed. Assign each region its test type to avoid mixing idle-target error with raised-RPM or recovery tests.

Comparison: Save a baseline, enter Compare mode and choose another region or the second simulated log. Comparability warnings are essential—particularly changes in CLT, target RPM or throttle/load.

Prototype boundary: No MLG or MSQ parser, automatic INI mapping, live ECU connection, real tune editing or ECU write is included. All example log data, tune values and diagnostic suggestions are synthetic.
Logger handoff · prototype

In EpicScope production this should pass the selected sample/time bounds into the real Logger, not create a second chart or a separate range authority.
Comparison setup

Choose independent baseline/candidate sources of the same test type. Identical/overlapping ranges are blocked. Comparability is assessed using qualified data and known logged conditions.

Production will additionally support choosing a separate real recording and retaining both log/tune identities.
